analysis: Reviewed the single changed unit, a Swift test file (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Distributed/DistributedInstalledLanesTests.swift, new test at lines 36-60). It only adds assertions about DistributedInstalledPlan lane selection: Gemma4 serial pipeline gets 4 lanes, lookahead and other modes/adapters keep the singleton default or nil, private-image requests get nil, and a cancelled Gemma lane retires alone (lanesRetireAlone). No production code, authentication, attestation, encryption, cache storage, or data-exposure path changes in this unit. The test encodes behavior from non-supplied production code (the gemma4PipelineBatchLanes constant, the prefillSchedule parameter, lanesRetireAlone), so the underlying implementation was not reviewed here. Security-relevant points for the integration pass: multi-lane batching of Gemma in a distributed pipeline raises concurrency and cross-request isolation questions (A-001, T-028 residual GPU/KV data, T-041 prefix-cache sharing across lanes, T-010 cancellation propagation). The tests encode that private images are excluded from lanes and that cancelled lanes retire alone, which is consistent with those threats. The production implementation in other batches should confirm per-lane KV/cache isolation and that cancellation actually frees only its own lane. No threat-model regression is identified in the test-only change.
